elements.title: DESIGN and DEVELOPMENT
elements.text: Conducts research, conceptualizes, designs, develops, and tests secure technology systems, including on perimeter and cloud-based networks.

elements.title: INVESTIGATION
elements.text: Investigates cybersecurity incidents and analyzes digital evidence to support internal, legal, or law-enforcement processes.

elements.title: IMPLEMENTATION and OPERATION
elements.text: Provides implementation, administration, configuration, operation, and maintenance to ensure effective and efficient technology system performance and security.

elements.title: OVERSIGHT and GOVERNANCE
elements.text: Provides leadership, management, direction, and advocacy so the organization may effectively manage cybersecurity-related risks to the enterprise and conduct cybersecurity work.

elements.title: PROTECTION and DEFENSE
elements.text: Protects against, identifies, and analyzes risks to technology systems or networks. Includes investigation of cybersecurity events or crimes related to technology systems and networks.

elements.title: Access Controls
elements.text: This Competency Area describes a learner’s capabilities to define, manage, and monitor the roles and secure access privileges of who is authorized to access protected data and resources and understand the impact of different types of access controls.

elements.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Security
elements.text: This Competency Area describes a learner’s capability to understand Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems and to use them in a secure manner that maximizes AI’s benefits while minimizing potential negative risks.

elements.title: Asset Management
elements.text: This Competency Area describes a learner’s capabilities to conduct and maintain an accurate inventory of all digital assets, to include identifying, developing, operating, maintaining, upgrading, and disposing of assets.

elements.title: Cloud Security
elements.text: This Competency Area describes a learner’s capabilities to protect cloud data, applications, and infrastructure from internal and external threats.

elements.title: Communications Security
elements.text: This Competency Area describes a learner’s capabilities to secure the transmissions, broadcasting, switching, control, and operation of communications and related network infrastructures.

elements.title: Cryptography
elements.text: This Competency Area describes a learner’s capabilities to transform data using cryptographic processes to ensure it can only be read by the person who is authorized to access it.

elements.title: Cyber Resiliency
elements.text: This Competency Area describes a learner’s capability related to architecting, designing, developing, implementing, and maintaining the trustworthiness of systems that use or are enabled by cyber resources in order to anticipate, withstand, recover from, and adapt to adverse conditions, stresses, attacks, or compromises.

elements.title: DevSecOps
elements.text: This Competency Area describes a learner’s capabilities to integrate security as a shared responsibility throughout the development, security, and operations (DevSecOps) life cycle of technologies.

elements.title: Operating Systems (OS) Security
elements.text: This Competency Area describes a learner’s capabilities to install, administer, troubleshoot, backup, and conduct recovery of Operating Systems (OS), including in simulated environments.

elements.title: Operational Technology (OT) Security
elements.text: This Competency Area describes a learner’s capabilities to improve and maintain the security of Operational Technology (OT) systems while addressing their unique performance, reliability, and safety requirements.

elements.title: Supply Chain Security
elements.text: This Competency Area describes a learner’s capabilities to analyze and control digital and physical risks presented by technology products or services purchased from parties outside your organization.

elements.title: Security Architect
elements.text: Responsible for designing the security of an organization's systems and technology architecture -- selecting controls, cryptography, and network and identity designs so security requirements are met by design.

elements.title: Security Engineer
elements.text: Responsible for building and maintaining the security of systems and infrastructure -- implementing and hardening controls, securing platforms and networks, and integrating security into how systems are designed, built, and run.

elements.title: Security Researcher
elements.text: Responsible for conducting software and systems engineering and software systems research to develop new capabilities with fully integrated cybersecurity. Conducts comprehensive technology research to evaluate potential vulnerabilities in technology systems.

elements.title: OT Security Engineer
elements.text: Responsible for working within the engineering department to design and create systems, processes, and procedures that maintain the safety, reliability, controllability and security of industrial systems in the face of intentional and incidental cyber events. Interfaces with Chief Information Security Officer, plant managers and industrial cybersecurity technicians.

elements.title: AI Security Engineer
elements.text: Responsible for evaluating and securing artificial intelligence and machine learning systems throughout their lifecycle -- assessing training data and model behavior for security and reliability risks, testing for adversarial vulnerabilities and unreliable or hallucinated outputs, and advising on the secure use and deployment of AI capabilities within the organization.

elements.title: Security Instructional Designer
elements.text: Responsible for developing, planning, coordinating, and evaluating cybersecurity awareness, training, or education content, methods, and techniques based on instructional needs and requirements.

elements.title: Security Instructor
elements.text: Responsible for developing and conducting cybersecurity awareness, training, or education.

elements.title: Cybersecurity Counsel
elements.text: Responsible for providing cybersecurity legal advice and recommendations, including monitoring related legislation and regulations.

elements.title: CISO
elements.text: Responsible for establishing vision and direction for an organization's cybersecurity operations and resources and their impact on digital and physical spaces. Possesses authority to make and execute decisions that impact an organization broadly, including policy approval and stakeholder engagement.

elements.title: Privacy Analyst
elements.text: Responsible for developing and overseeing an organization’s privacy compliance program and staff, including establishing and managing privacy-related governance, policy, and incident response needs.

elements.title: Security Program Manager
elements.text: Responsible for planning, running, and reporting on security programs and projects -- scope, budget, schedule, priorities, vendors, and the people and skills the program needs.

elements.title: IT Auditor
elements.text: Responsible for conducting independent comprehensive assessments of management, operational, and technical security controls and control enhancements employed within or inherited by a system to determine their overall effectiveness.

elements.title: Third-Party Risk Analyst
elements.text: Responsible for developing cybersecurity supply chain risk management (C-SCRM) policies, processes, and procedures to identify, assess, protect against, and respond to cybersecurity risks throughout the supply chain, and for advising other stakeholders within an enterprise about supply chain risks.

elements.title: SOC Analyst
elements.text: Responsible for monitoring, detecting, and triaging security events and alerts across an organization's systems and networks, and escalating and responding to confirmed threats.

elements.title: Digital Forensics Analyst
elements.text: Responsible for collecting, preserving, and analyzing digital evidence from computers, networks, and devices to investigate incidents and support internal, legal, or law-enforcement processes.

elements.title: Incident Responder
elements.text: Responsible for investigating, analyzing, and responding to network cybersecurity incidents.

elements.title: Insider Risk Analyst
elements.text: Responsible for identifying and assessing the capabilities and activities of cybersecurity insider threats; produces findings that support internal investigations, HR, legal, and -- where applicable -- law enforcement.

elements.title: Threat Intelligence Analyst
elements.text: Responsible for collecting and analyzing information about threat actors, their tools, and their techniques, and turning it into intelligence that helps the organization anticipate, detect, and respond to attacks.

elements.title: Vulnerability Management Analyst
elements.text: Responsible for assessing systems and networks to identify deviations from acceptable configurations, network-segment policy, or local policy. Measures effectiveness of defense-in-depth architecture against known vulnerabilities.

elements.title: Penetration Tester
elements.text: Responsible for simulating adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures against systems and networks -- including evading detection by defensive controls -- to identify exploitable weaknesses and report findings that help the organization improve its security posture.

elements.title: Malware Analyst
elements.text: Responsible for analyzing malicious software and other suspicious artifacts to understand their behavior, capabilities, and origin -- using static and dynamic analysis and reverse engineering techniques to support detection, containment, and threat intelligence efforts.

elements.text: Responsible for building, testing, and tuning the detections that alert on attacker behavior, validating coverage against known techniques and working with red teams to close gaps.

elements.title: Threat Hunter
elements.text: Responsible for proactively searching systems and networks for attackers who evaded existing defenses, forming hypotheses from threat intelligence and testing them against telemetry.

elements.title: Application Security Engineer
elements.text: Responsible for securing software throughout its lifecycle -- building security into code and design, reviewing code and architecture for weaknesses, testing applications for vulnerabilities, and driving the fixes.

elements.title: DevSecOps Engineer
elements.text: Responsible for building security into software delivery pipelines and platforms, automating checks so code and infrastructure ship securely by default.

elements.title: GRC Analyst
elements.text: Responsible for governance, risk, and compliance work -- writing and maintaining security policies, assessing risk, mapping controls to frameworks, and monitoring ongoing compliance.

elements.title: Security Awareness Manager
elements.text: Responsible for building the training, phishing simulations, and communication that help employees recognize and report threats and reduce human risk.

elements.title: Cyber Range Engineer
elements.text: Responsible for designing, building, and operating simulated environments for security training, exercises, and testing, combining infrastructure engineering with attack and defense scenarios.
